description: The true path of the fixture (The Vestry Cup; `at` lists what must have been read), question by question: each move serves the one question in its `for_q`, and a seed's order of solving is played (scripts/path-check.mjs). Amos is placed by the tower stair, the key by the key book, Mr. Vane by the note from the Grange; then the cup, with the survey's one door.

moves.see: went up the tower stair at six
moves.why: I saw him go up at six.

moves.see: the only way up or down
moves.why: And the stair is the only way, and it comes down where I sat.
So he was up the tower the whole time.

moves.see: signed the vestry key out at half past seven
moves.why: The key book has Miss Dent taking the key at half past seven.
And bringing it back at a quarter past eight; nobody else signed for it.
So Hester Dent had the key that evening.
Mrs. Holt sat with him at the Grange from five until half past nine.
So he was at the Grange all evening.

moves.see: it went between six and nine
moves.why: I locked the cup away at six myself.

moves.see: the only way into the vestry is its door
moves.why: The windows are barred, so whoever took it came in by the door, with the key.
Amos was up the tower and Mr. Vane at the Grange; Hester Dent had the key.
